name: NodeCraft
author: João Santos
texts: NodeCraft is a self-hosted, distributed game server hosting platform built entirely from scratch. Acting as a control plane for multiplayer games like Minecraft, Hytale, and Terraria, it orchestrates a fleet of worker machines to create, configure, and monitor servers through a single web interface.

The architecture consists of three independent services: a central Manager API that handles authentication, resource quotas, and scheduling; a React-powered Web Panel for users; and a distributed Worker fleet that runs actual game instances in fully isolated Docker containers.

NodeCraft features a real-time console streaming over WebSockets, a complete web-based file manager, and granular per-instance permissions. It also automates critical infrastructure tasks, such as running nightly scheduled backups to S3-compatible cloud storage.

This flagship project demonstrates my ability to engineer complex, highly scalable distributed systems. By bridging low-level container orchestration with a polished full-stack interface, NodeCraft showcases a robust, production-ready solution.

name: PedePizza
author: João Santos
texts: PedePizza is a modern, responsive e-commerce platform tailored for pizza delivery. Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and a robust Node.js REST API, it delivers a seamless, cross-device user experience.

The frontend features an intuitive interface where users can dynamically browse menus, customize their orders with specific ingredients, and manage a real-time shopping cart through to a frictionless checkout process.

Under the hood, the backend is powered by Node.js and Express, ensuring fast and secure order management. It integrates deeply with MongoDB to handle persistent data storage for user preferences and order histories.
This project showcases my ability to design and implement end-to-end web applications, combining a highly interactive UI with a scalable backend architecture.

name: Snake
author: João Santos
texts: As one of my first HTML projects, WebSnake represents an early stage of my journey into web development and helped me build a strong foundation in frontend programming and JavaScript.
WebSnake is a classic arcade Snake game reimagined for the browser, built entirely with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, ensuring smooth performance across devices.
The custom game engine features real-time collision detection, dynamic growth mechanics, and application state management, providing players with an engaging and nostalgic experience.
An intuitive grid-based movement system and real-time score tracking were implemented to challenge users as the gameplay speed progressively increases.
This project demonstrates my strong grasp of core JavaScript logic, DOM manipulation, game loop fundamentals, and event handling without relying on external libraries.

name: SmartWiki
author: João Santos
texts: SmartWiki is a hybrid informational and e-commerce platform focused on smart city innovations and IoT technologies, built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Bootstrap.

The platform serves as an educational hub, allowing users to explore detailed articles and guides about sustainable urban solutions, while seamlessly integrating a storefront for related smart devices.

Designed with a mobile-first approach, it features an intuitive UI complete with dynamic search capabilities, custom wishlists, and a streamlined purchasing flow for an effortless shopping experience.
SmartWiki effectively merges educational content with a functional digital storefront, highlighting my skills in building accessible, feature-rich platforms using modern frontend frameworks.

name: Culturafro
author: João Santos
texts: CulturaFro is a responsive website developed with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, created for a group of friends as part of a high school project focused on African culture and its influence on Brazilian society.
I designed and developed the website based on the project's educational goals, transforming their concept into an accessible and engaging digital experience.

The platform explores topics related to African traditions, history, cultural heritage, and their contributions to Brazilian society, encouraging users to learn more about this important part of Brazil's cultural identity.
The website features a clean and intuitive interface designed to provide a consistent experience across different devices and make the content easy to navigate and explore.

CulturaFro was an early opportunity for me to develop a website around a real-world brief, strengthening my frontend development skills while demonstrating how web technologies can be used to communicate ideas and promote cultural awareness.

name: Phoenix
author: João Santos
texts: Phoenix is a responsive news website developed with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Bootstrap, created for a group of friends as part of a middle school project focused on smart cities in Brazil.
I designed and developed the website based on their project concept, turning their research and ideas into a structured digital news platform.
The platform covers topics such as sustainability, technology, infrastructure, and security, presenting information about innovations and developments related to smart cities in Brazil.

Built with a responsive and intuitive interface, Phoenix provides a consistent browsing experience across different devices, making it easy for users to navigate through articles and explore the content.

This project gave me an opportunity to develop a complete website around an external project brief, further strengthening my frontend development skills and my ability to translate ideas and requirements into functional digital experiences.
